blogPosts.title: How Much Does Concrete Floor Polishing Cost in South Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A complete breakdown of concrete polishing costs in South Melbourne. Learn what affects the price per square metre and how to budget for your project.
body: If you're looking to polish a concrete floor in South Melbourne, you're probably wondering what it's going to cost. Prices vary based on floor condition, size, and finish level. On average, residential polished concrete runs between $50 and $90 per square metre. Commercial projects can be slightly different due to scale and access.

The biggest factor is the starting condition of your slab. A new concrete slab that's already smooth will cost less because it needs fewer grinding steps. Old or damaged concrete requires more aggressive grinding and patching, which adds to the labour. Our team at Nazcrete always does a thorough inspection first to give you an accurate price.

The grind level also affects cost. A basic 'grind and seal' with a 200-grit finish is cheaper than a high-gloss polish to 3000 grit. For homes, we often recommend a medium polish that balances shine and cost. For commercial spaces, a high-gloss finish can increase durability and reflect light, reducing lighting costs.

Don't forget extras like colour staining, anti-slip additives, or decorative aggregates. Staining costs around $15-$25 per square metre extra. Anti-slip is about $5 per square metre. These additions are worth considering if you have wet areas or want a unique look.

One hidden cost many people overlook is floor removal. If you have old carpet, vinyl, or tiles, removing them adds $10-$30 per square metre depending on the material. Nazcrete includes removal in your quote when needed, so everything is transparent from the start.

The best way to get an accurate price is to have us come to your South Melbourne property. We'll test the concrete, measure up, and give you a fixed quote. No call-out fee, no obligation. Give Nazcrete a ring on 0413 948 228 and we'll sort you out.

blogPosts.title: Epoxy Flooring vs Polished Concrete: Which Is Better for Your Melbourne Garage?
blogPosts.excerpt: Comparing epoxy coatings and polished concrete for garage floors. Which offers better durability, slip resistance, and value for Melbourne homeowners?
body: Melbourne garage floors take a beating. Oil drips, tyre marks, moisture, and heavy equipment. Two popular options are epoxy coatings and polished concrete. Both have their strengths, but they suit different needs. Let's break it down for your South Melbourne garage.

Epoxy coatings create a thick, glossy layer on top of the concrete. They're highly resistant to chemicals and are easy to clean. You can choose from dozens of colours and even add decorative flakes. However, epoxy can peel or chip if the concrete underneath is not perfectly prepared or if moisture seeps through from below.

Polished concrete, on the other hand, is the concrete itself ground down and sealed. There's nothing to peel because the finish is part of the slab. It's incredibly durable and resistant to tyre marks. It also handles moisture better than epoxy because the concrete can still breathe through the densifier and sealer.

Cost-wise, epoxy is often cheaper per square metre initially ($40-$70) versus polished concrete ($55-$90). But epoxy may need recoating every 5-7 years, whereas polished concrete can last the life of the slab with occasional resealing. Over the long term, polished concrete often wins on value.

For Melbourne's climate, polished concrete handles temperature changes well. Epoxy can yellow or become brittle under UV light if the garage has windows. For indoor garages, both work fine. If you park a car regularly, polished concrete resists tyre marking better than epoxy.

At Nazcrete, we've installed both in South Melbourne garages. For a workshop or home gym where you might drop tools, polished concrete is more impact-resistant. For a showroom or decorative space, epoxy can look amazing. We always advise based on your actual use. Give us a call and we'll talk it through.

blogPosts.title: Concrete Grinding vs Resurfacing: What's the Difference for Melbourne Homes?
blogPosts.excerpt: Understand when to grind and when to resurface your concrete floors. A practical guide for homeowners in South Melbourne and surrounding suburbs.
body: Concrete grinding and resurfacing are two different processes, but they're often confused. Grinding involves using diamond abrasives to remove a thin layer of concrete. It levels uneven slabs, removes old coatings, and opens the pores for sealing. Resurfacing adds a new layer of cementitious material on top of the existing concrete.

When should you grind? If your floor is relatively sound but has minor imperfections, a few millimetres of grinding can transform it. It's perfect for polishing, as you want to expose fresh concrete. Grinding is also great for removing old epoxy or adhesive residues from floor removal.

Resurfacing is better for floors with deeper cracks, pitting, or severe wear. A resurfacing product bonds to the old concrete and gives you a new surface layer. It can also be used to change the colour or texture completely. However, resurfacing adds thickness, which might affect door clearances.

In South Melbourne, we see many older homes with concrete floors that have been covered with carpet or vinyl for decades. Once we remove the covering, we often find a mix of issues. Sometimes grinding is enough; other times a full resurfacing is needed. Our inspection process determines the best path.

Cost difference: grinding for polishing typically runs $50-$80 per square metre. Resurfacing starts around $60 per square metre but can go higher for custom finishes. Resurfacing also takes longer because the new layer needs to cure before it can be sealed.

If you're unsure, call Nazcrete. We'll come to your South Melbourne home, assess the floor, and give you honest advice. No upselling, just the right solution for your concrete. We've done this for hundreds of Melbourne homes and know what works.

blogPosts.title: Floor Removal in Melbourne: What to Expect When Stripping Old Carpet or Vinyl
blogPosts.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to professional floor removal in Melbourne. Learn how Nazcrete handles carpet, vinyl, and tile removal before concrete polishing.
body: Before you can polish or epoxy a concrete floor, you often need to remove the old floor covering. In Melbourne homes, that's usually carpet, vinyl, or ceramic tiles. Floor removal seems straightforward, but there are tricks to doing it cleanly and safely without damaging the concrete underneath.

Carpet removal is the easiest. We cut it into strips, roll it up, and remove the underlay. The tricky part is the adhesive left behind. Old glue can be stubborn and may require a specialised grinding step before polishing. Nazcrete includes that in our process so the final floor is perfectly smooth.

Vinyl flooring can be sheet vinyl or vinyl tiles. Some old vinyl contains asbestos, especially in homes built before 1990. We test suspect material before starting. If asbestos is present, we follow strict removal protocols. Our team is trained in safe handling and disposal.

Ceramic tile removal is the most labour-intensive. Tiles are brittle and can shatter, but we use tools that minimise dust and noise. The thin-set mortar underneath also needs to be ground down if you want a polished concrete finish. This adds to the time but ensures a clean result.

Once the floor covering is gone, we inspect the concrete for cracks, dampness, and level. Often the concrete has been hidden for decades. We patch, grind, and prepare it for whatever finish you've chosen. A proper removal job sets the stage for a floor that looks brand new.

Nazcrete handles the entire process from removal to final polish. We serve South Melbourne and all Melbourne suburbs. Call us on 0413 948 228 for a free quote. We'll walk you through what's involved and give you a fixed price with no surprises.
